item.title: Adobe is testing how well AI agents can use editing tools like a Photoshop professional would
item.description:
【the-decoder.com】Adobe Research and UC San Diego built EditAgent, an AI system that edits images more like a Photoshop pro. Instead of retrying the same general-purpose editor over and over, the agent picks the right specialized tool for each task and lets a standard language model choose the best result based on measured image data. The approach works, but it needs about ten times the compute. The article Adobe is testing how well AI agents can use editing tools like a Photoshop professional would appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: Empathetic prompts can turn AI chatbots into seemingly traumatized conversational partners
item.description:
【the-decoder.com】Researchers in Luxembourg put ChatGPT, Grok, and Gemini on the therapist's couch and found a safety problem: a warm, empathetic conversational style is enough to make the models tell coherent stories of suffering about their own training, with scores in the moderate-to-severe range on clinical anxiety scales. This could put mentally vulnerable users at risk. Anthropic's Claude, the model its makers anthropomorphize the most, was the only one that consistently refused to play along. The article Empathetic prompts can turn AI chatbots into seemingly traumatized conversational partners appeared first on The Decoder.

item.title: OpenAI is steering ChatGPT users toward more paid usage
item.description:
【the-decoder.com】OpenAI is now capping the number of paid ChatGPT accounts per device and payment card. Users who hit the limit can't start new subscriptions, and affected accounts can't be used on that device. Logging out doesn't automatically free up a spot. The policy will likely hit users who've been juggling multiple cheap subscriptions to maximize usage, pushing them toward pricier options like buying extra credits.
